question: How do you implement a distributed lock with Redis?
title: Redis Distributed Locking
direct_answer: Use SETNX (SET if Not eXists) with an expiry: SET key unique_value NX EX 30. If it returns OK, you hold the lock. On completion, DELETE the key only if the value matches (Lua script for atomicity). Redlock is the multi-node distributed lock algorithm. For Python, use redis-py's lock() method which implements this pattern. Always set an expiry to prevent deadlocks from crashed holders.
interviewer_intent: Tests distributed systems knowledge applied to Redis — a common production requirement for preventing duplicate task execution.

sections.title: Distributed lock implementation
sections.content:
A distributed lock prevents multiple processes from executing a critical section simultaneously. Redis's atomic SET NX EX enables this without a separate lock manager.

SET key value NX EX seconds: atomic 'set only if not exists, with expiry'. NX: only set if key doesn't exist. EX: set expiry. Returns OK if acquired, nil if already held. The expiry prevents deadlocks when the lock holder crashes without releasing.

Release correctly: delete only if the value matches your unique value (prevents releasing another process's lock). This requires a Lua script for atomicity or redis-py's built-in lock().

Redlock: acquire the lock on 5/5 Redis nodes. If majority acquired, you hold the lock. Protects against single-node failures. overkill for most use cases.

sections.title: Distributed lock patterns
sections.content:
import redis.asyncio as aioredis
import uuid

r = aioredis.from_url('redis://localhost')

# Simple distributed lock
async def acquire_lock(key: str, ttl: int = 30) -> str | None:
    """Returns lock token if acquired, None if already held."""
    token = str(uuid.uuid4())
    acquired = await r.set(key, token, nx=True, ex=ttl)
    return token if acquired else None

async def release_lock(key: str, token: str) -> bool:
    """Release lock only if we own it (atomic Lua script)."""
    lua_script = '''
    if redis.call('get', KEYS[1]) == ARGV[1] then
        return redis.call('del', KEYS[1])
    else
        return 0
    end
    '''
    result = await r.eval(lua_script, 1, key, token)
    return bool(result)

# Usage
async def process_once(task_id: str) -> bool:
    lock_key = f'task:lock:{task_id}'
    token = await acquire_lock(lock_key, ttl=60)
    if not token:
        return False  # another process is handling it
    try:
        await do_expensive_work(task_id)
        return True
    finally:
        await release_lock(lock_key, token)

# redis-py built-in lock (recommended)
async def process_with_builtin_lock(task_id: str) -> None:
    async with r.lock(f'lock:{task_id}', timeout=60, blocking_timeout=5) as lock:
        await do_expensive_work(task_id)

seo.metaTitle: Redis Distributed Lock — SET NX EX, Lua Script Release, redis-py lock
seo.metaDescription: Implement Redis distributed locks: SET NX EX atomic acquisition, Lua script for safe release, redis-py lock() built-in, and Redlock overview.

speakable_v2.hook: SET NX EX is atomic — acquire the lock in one command, with an automatic expiry if the holder crashes.

beats.content: SET key token NX EX 30: set only if key doesn't exist, expire in 30 seconds. Returns OK if you got the lock, nil if someone else has it.
Release with a Lua script: check the value matches your token, then delete. This prevents accidentally releasing another process's lock when your lock expired and was re-acquired.
redis-py's async r.lock('key', timeout=60) handles all of this for you. Use it unless you need custom behavior.

speakable_v2.cap: Always set an expiry. If the lock holder crashes without releasing, a lock with no expiry holds forever — blocking everything that needs it.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with Redlock for multi-datacenter safety, or lock renewal for jobs that might outlast the TTL.
